answer: An agent garden can resist Sybil attacks through hardware-enforced remote attestation. Participants operate within a secure enclave whose cryptographic kernel signs identity proofs using factory-fused silicon keys. This erects a sturdy juniper barrier against automated cloning, forcing attackers to incur the verifiable cost of procuring physical microchips per identity. However, this relies on centralized chip vendors, and enclave side-channel exploits can compromise identity guarantees.
